title: Next.js-Powered AI Platform for Smart Expense Tracking, Budgeting and Insights
authors: Badiger, R.; R, R.; Moraas, T.; Naik, V.G.; Karthikeyan, A.N.
tldr: Spend AI is a full-stack Next.js platform integrating XGBoost transaction categorization, Gemini LLM financial insights, and Prophet time-series forecasting to automate personal finance management.
problem_and_motivation: India's digital payment ecosystem generates enormous volumes of transaction data across multiple channels, yet individuals lack unified intelligent tools to synthesize this information. Existing personal finance tools either require manual data entry or remain inaccessible as enterprise-grade solutions, with limited personalization and opaque recommendation logic.
approach: XGBoost gradient-boosted classifier trained on labelled transactions augmented with synthetic data for multi-class categorization into eighteen spending categories.
Gemini LLM queried via retrieval-augmented generation pattern, injecting user-specific spending summaries and budget utilization into structured prompts.
Prophet time-series model decomposing historical spending into trend, seasonality, and holiday components for monthly expenditure forecasting.
Five-layer modular architecture separating Presentation, Business Logic, AI, Data, and Authentication concerns with Next.js 14 Server Actions.
Anomaly detection flagging transactions exceeding 2.5 standard deviations from category-level means to feed insight generation.
User override events logged and used to update category priors in a lightweight online learning loop for personalization.
Supabase PostgreSQL with row-level security enforcing per-user data isolation at the database level.
Evaluation on held-out test set of 4,200 transactions from anonymized personal finance datasets.
findings: num: 91.3% weighted F1-score for XGBoost transaction categorization across eighteen categories on a 4,200-transaction test set.
num: 78% reduction in manual expense-logging effort compared to conventional approaches.
num: 84% of pilot participants found AI-generated insights useful or very useful.
num: High-frequency categories (Food and Dining, Transport, Utilities) achieve F1-scores above 0.95.
num: Miscellaneous category shows lower precision at 0.81 due to high linguistic diversity.
num: 420ms average server response time for standard dashboard loads.
num: AI insight generation via Gemini API adds 800 to 1,400ms additional latency.
num: Cold-start problem causes lower accuracy for new users with fewer than 50 historical transactions.
key_figures_tables: Figure 1: End-to-end user workflow showing seven-stage process from authentication to budget alerts -> Illustrates complete data flow through the system.
Figure 2: Five-layer modular architecture diagram -> Presentation, Business Logic, AI, Data, and Authentication layers enable independent scaling.
Figure 3: Technology stack overview -> Shows integration of Next.js 14, Prisma, Supabase, Clerk, Gemini, XGBoost, and Prophet.
Figure 4: AI Insight Generation pipeline using RAG pattern -> User financial aggregates injected into Gemini prompts to ground outputs in real data.
Figure 5: XGBoost transaction categorization F1-scores by category -> Quantifies per-category model performance on the test set.

definitions.definition: Large Language Model, a generative AI model capable of processing and generating natural language text.
Extreme Gradient Boosting, a gradient-boosted decision tree classifier used for supervised classification tasks.
Meta's decomposable time-series forecasting model that separates trend, seasonality, and holiday effects.
Retrieval-Augmented Generation, a prompting technique that injects retrieved data into LLM context to reduce hallucination.
Row-Level Security, a database-level access control mechanism enforcing per-user data isolation.
A schema-first ORM for type-safe database access and automated migration management with PostgreSQL.
An identity management SDK providing authentication via email and Google OAuth with multi-factor support.
A UI component library built on Radix UI primitives for accessible, pre-built interface elements.
Explainable Artificial Intelligence, techniques such as SHAP and LIME that interpret model predictions.
Conditional Tabular GAN, a synthetic data generation technique for producing realistic tabular datasets.
Optical Character Recognition, technology for extracting text from images such as receipt scans.
Digital Personal Data Protection Act, India's regulatory framework for personal data privacy.
Small and Medium Enterprise, a business classification relevant to transaction categorization benchmarks.
Unified Payments Interface, India's real-time mobile payment system facilitating billions of monthly transactions.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Spend AI contributes an open, production-grade full-stack architecture that unifies XGBoost-based transaction categorization, LLM-powered financial insights via retrieval-augmented generation, and Prophet time-series forecasting within a single deployable platform. The work bridges the gap between research prototypes and commercial opacity by providing a transparent, modular five-layer architecture. It provides empirical evaluation of Gemini's suitability for consumer-facing financial advisory tasks in the Indian digital payment context. The platform introduces user override feedback loops for ongoing category prior personalization, demonstrating practical online learning in a financial application.
directly_justifies: num: XGBoost achieves 91.3% weighted F1-score for transaction categorization across eighteen spending categories.
Existing consumer PFM tools rarely combine automated ML categorization with LLM natural-language insights in a single platform.
Gemini LLM demonstrates competitive capability for financial advisory tasks compared to GPT-4 and other leading models.
Cold-start problem causes lower categorization accuracy for users with fewer than 50 historical transactions.
num: Manual expense-logging effort reduced by approximately 78% compared to conventional approaches.
limits: Prophet forecasting requires at least 3 months of historical data; shorter histories yield wider confidence intervals.
Direct banking API integration is absent, requiring users to manually enter or import transaction data.
LLM hallucination risk remains despite RAG-style prompt grounding; financial guidance may be imprecise.
Privacy and regulatory compliance under the Indian DPDP Act require further attention beyond Supabase RLS controls.
No explainable AI integration for categorization predictions, though SHAP-based XAI is proposed as future work.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All fourteen topic domains were systematically scanned for relevance. Domain 4 (Landscape of Existing Personal Finance Systems) was flagged as high relevance, with 4.A covering the comprehensive literature review of PFM platforms and 4.B capturing the three specific gaps the paper identifies. Domain 5 (Financial Behavioral Profiles) was partially relevant at medium level through 5.B's cold-start acknowledgment, though the paper does not develop behavioral profiles per se. Domain 8 (Anomaly Detection) was selected across three codes: 8.A at medium relevance for the 2.5-sigma threshold detection system, 8.B at low relevance since the detection method is statistical rather than algorithmic, and 8.C at contextual relevance as cold-start is mentioned but no baseline strategy is proposed. Domain 9 (Mobile-First Design) was included at low for 9.A (design principles not the focus) and medium for 9.B (responsive dashboard UX). Domain 14 (ML Model Serving) was selected at medium through 14.B for the XGBoost deployment architecture. Domains 1-3 (Filipino demographics and expense categorization frameworks) were rejected as the paper focuses on Indian users and does not propose new categorization ontologies. Domains 6-7 (Predictive Modeling algorithms and Budgeting Optimization) were considered but rejected since Prophet is used off-the-shelf rather than as a novel contribution, and no constrained budget optimization is presented. Domains 10-13 (Privacy, Engagement, Evaluation, Savings/Debt) were considered but lack sufficient depth in the paper to warrant topic codes.

limitations: Cold-start accuracy degradation for users with fewer than 50 historical transactions is acknowledged.
LLM hallucination risk in financial guidance is acknowledged despite RAG mitigation.
Absence of direct banking API integration limits automatic data capture.
Time-series forecasting requires minimum three months of historical data for reliable predictions.
No direct comparison with alternative ML categorization algorithms beyond citing prior work.
Anomaly detection limited to simple statistical thresholds without adaptive or context-aware mechanisms.
